Loop Tuner

Tune a feedback loop by trying controller settings side by side. Each row in Candidates is one controller; its response is drawn on the scope in the same colour. The hatched areas are the limits from your Goal: a candidate that stays out of them is feasible (✓), and the feasible one with the lowest score is marked BEST.

Working with it

↑ ↓Step through the candidates SpaceShow or hide the selected candidate on the scope NDuplicate the selected candidate, to try a variation DelDelete the selected candidate TAuto-tune: search the gains for the best feasible score 1 … 7Jump to a module: reference, controller, actuator, disturbance, plant, sensor, noise PPlay or pause the scan sweep Ctrl Z / Ctrl Shift ZUndo / redo

Knobs: drag up or down (hold Shift for fine steps), scroll, or use the arrow keys. Double-click a knob to reset it; click its value to type one. Gains that can be switched off read “off” at the bottom of their travel.

The controller module edits the selected candidate. Every other module is shared by all candidates, so changing the plant shows how every controller copes with it. Changing a block’s type keeps the parameters both types share, and switching back restores the rest.

Files

The whole project is one JSON document. Save JSON and Open read and write it; you can also drop a file on the page or paste JSON. Export HTML writes this page with the project inside, ready to send to someone.

For agents

The same simulation runs in Node. With the project file (or an exported HTML file):

node cli.mjs eval project.json          # metrics, score and feasibility of every candidate
node cli.mjs try project.json --type PID --set Kp=2 --set Ki=0.8 --set Kd=1 --save
node cli.mjs tune project.json --from "Z–N PID" --save
node cli.mjs html project.json -o shared.html

In the browser, window.loopTuner offers getProject(), setProject(p), evaluate(), select(name) and addCandidate(c).
